panels.rationale: Histopathology image (H&E stain) from a deep excisional biopsy of a lower extremity lesion showing classic features of erythema induratum of Bazin: lobular panniculitis with granulomatous inflammation, caseating fat necrosis, vasculitis, and Langhans giant cells.
panels.attribution_text: Gonzalez Quiroz et al. Erythema Induratum of Bazin Associated With a Negative Tuberculin Test: A Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.113542. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological study of subcutaneous tissue stained with hematoxylin-eosin (H&E), showing a pattern of lobular panniculitis, characterized by predominant inflammatory infiltrate in the adipose tissue lobules, with relative preservation of the interlobular septa and vasculitis (original magnifications ×100). Subcutaneous adipose tissue was observed with a predominantly lobular inflammatory infiltrate and alteration of the normal adipose architecture. The inflammatory infiltrate was composed mainly of mononuclear inflammatory cells and histiocytes, with focal areas of adipocyte degeneration and fat necrosis. Associated fibrotic and inflammatory changes were observed in the subcutaneous tissue, along with vasculitis consistent with lobular panniculitis.

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph from a case report of erythema induratum of Bazin showing multiple necrotic ulcers with violaceous halos and perilesional induration on the lower extremities, consistent with the disease's characteristic cutaneous manifestations.
panels.attribution_text: Gonzalez Quiroz et al. Erythema Induratum of Bazin Associated With a Negative Tuberculin Test: A Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.113542. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Lower extremities with multiple necrotic ulcers of irregular sizes and shapes. Extensive ulcerated plaque on the posterior aspect of the right leg, covered by a necrotic eschar with irregular and raised borders, surrounded by an erythematous-violaceous halo and perilesional induration. Smaller satellite ulcers with hemorrhagic and necrotic crusts are also observed.
in_text_mentions: ules associated with edema and increased local temperature. Several of these lesions showed poorly defined central ulceration and eschar remnants. An extensive erythematous area was also observed on the left leg, with signs suggestive of incipient necrosis. Multiple deep subcutaneous nodules consistent with panniculitis were also identified. In the lower right extremity, in the posterior region of the knee, an extensive ulcer was observed measuring approximately 15 × 10 centimeters, with irregular contours and poorly defined edges, exposing the subcutaneous tissue and deeper planes (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). B: Clinical photograph showing characteristic nodular lesions of Erythema Induratum of Bazin on the dorsal aspect of the lower limbs. C: Clinical photograph showing a violaceous nodular lesion on the right forearm consistent with the cutaneous manifestations of Erythema Induratum of Bazin.
